# ============================================================================
# Python environment for "Statistics for Bioinformatics"
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pinned to lower bounds that are known to contain every API used in the
# course scripts. Build the image with:
#     docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.python -t learn-stats-py:1.0 .
# Nothing is installed on the host; every package lives inside the container.
# ============================================================================

# --- Numerical / array core -------------------------------------------------
numpy>=1.26,<3            # n-dimensional arrays, linear algebra, RNG (Generator API)
scipy>=1.11,<2            # distributions, optimisation, hypothesis tests, linalg

# --- Data handling ----------------------------------------------------------
pandas>=2.1,<3            # DataFrame / Series, groupby, tidy reshaping

# --- Plotting ---------------------------------------------------------------
matplotlib>=3.8,<4        # all figures in the course
seaborn>=0.13,<1          # statistical graphics convenience layer

# --- Statistical modelling --------------------------------------------------
statsmodels>=0.14,<1      # OLS/GLM/GEE/MixedLM, multipletests, power, survival
scikit-learn>=1.3,<2      # CV, pipelines, penalised regression, metrics, PCA
lifelines>=0.27,<1        # Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, Cox PH with clean formula API

# --- Literate programming ---------------------------------------------------
jupytext>=1.16,<2         # .py (percent format) <-> .ipynb round trip
nbformat>=5.9,<6          # notebook object model
nbclient>=0.9,<1          # headless notebook execution (used by the test runner)
nbconvert>=7.10,<8        # notebook -> HTML export
ipykernel>=6.25,<7        # the kernel the notebooks execute against
jupyterlab>=4.0,<5        # interactive front-end (optional for batch runs)
